title: Air Canada AC5 arrives
notes: Inbound flight added by the audit. Confirm the operating terminal in the Air Canada app before travel.

title: Arrival dinner & breakfast supplies
notes: Keep dinner flexible for immigration delays. Buy breakfast and water for the next early start if hotel food service has ended.

title: Set up 4 IC cards · Suica / PASMO
notes: One adult IC card per traveler. Use for ordinary JR, subways, private railways and buses. Load modest balances and top up as needed. This does not replace reserved Shinkansen or N’EX tickets.

title: Narita Express → Tokyo Station
notes: Buy or rebook only after immigration and baggage. All seats are reserved; take the next practical N’EX rather than risking a missed fixed train.

title: Tokyo Station → Shiomi Station
notes: Follow the long internal signs to the JR Keiyo Line, allow 15–20 minutes to transfer, then ride 3 stops to Shiomi. Earlier/later Keiyo trains are frequent.

title: Reserve every intercity train
notes: Book Aug 10, 14, 16 and 19 seats together now. Nozomi is reserved-seat-only Aug 7–16. Reserve oversized-baggage seats for any bag measuring 161–250 cm on three sides.

title: Tokyo Bay Shiomi Prince Hotel
notes: Locked hotel · add confirmation number.

title: Prebooked taxi → Senso-ji
notes: Leave the Shiomi hotel lobby at 05:10. If the taxi is absent, call the dispatcher and request GO immediately. At 05:20 switch to the first JR Keiyo service from Shiomi, continue by subway and begin Senso-ji around 06:20; shorten the river stop.

title: Senso-ji Temple & Nakamise
notes: See Kaminarimon, the temple grounds and the quiet approach before tour groups. The main hall opens at 06:00; most Nakamise shops open later.

title: Sumida River & Skytree views
notes: Walk the riverfront for open views of Tokyo Skytree while the morning is cool. This is a ground-level photo stop, not another observation deck.

title: Yanaka & Nezu Shrine
notes: Required eastern-Tokyo stop. Visit Nezu Shrine and the quiet Yanaka lanes early; most Yanaka shops will not yet be open.

title: Breakfast & cooling stop
notes: Eat near Asakusa, then start Kappabashi close to store opening time.

title: Kappabashi Kitchen Town
notes: Browse specialist knife, ceramics, cookware and realistic food-model shops. Many stores open around 10:00, so do not schedule this at dawn.

title: Tokyo Skytree Town & Solamachi
notes: Explore Solamachi, character shops and the tower base. The paid Skytree deck is intentionally skipped because Shibuya Sky and Tokyo Tower are the selected views.

title: Tokyo National Museum
notes:
Japan’s strongest broad collection of Japanese art, armour, sculpture and historical objects. Regular collection admission is paid but does not normally require advance booking.

Saved note from the earlier calendar: Two-hour focused visit to the strongest Japanese galleries. Use the online adult tickets to bypass the sales counter.

title: Ueno Park
notes: Required handwritten-list stop between the museum and Ameyoko.

title: Ameyoko Market
notes: Required handwritten-list stop. Market lanes and snacks on the direct route toward Akihabara.

title: Akihabara
notes: Moved into the first Tokyo stay to keep eastern Tokyo together. Electronics, games, arcades, gachapon and collectables; Hareruya2 is scheduled inside this block.

title: Hareruya2 Akihabara Tower
location: 1-2-13 Sotokanda · 3 min from Electric Town Exit
notes: Required Hareruya2 stop within the Akihabara block: six floors of Pokémon cards and a large play space. Official hours currently extend late.

title: Akihabara dinner break
notes: Take a seated dinner break during the late shopping block.

title: Tokyo National Museum · online adult tickets
notes: Counter-bypass only, not express entry. Buy adult QR tickets online; general admission is free for both teens under 18 with proof of age.

title: Prebooked taxi → Meiji Jingu
notes: Leave the Shiomi hotel lobby at 04:55. If the taxi is absent, call the dispatcher and request GO. At 05:15 walk to Shiomi for the first JR service, continue via Tokyo Station and begin Meiji Jingu around 06:15; shorten Yoyogi/breakfast.

title: Meiji Shrine
notes: Walk the forested approach and shrine precinct before the heat and crowds. August opening is 05:00.

title: Breakfast near Harajuku
notes: Use the quiet gap before shops open for breakfast and hydration.

title: Harajuku, Omotesando & Cat Street
notes: Walk Takeshita Street before peak crowds, then Omotesando architecture and Cat Street as shops begin opening.

title: Shibuya PARCO & Nintendo Tokyo
notes:
Nintendo Tokyo opens at 10:00 and may distribute same-day numbered entry tickets on this busy Saturday. Check official instructions that morning.

Saved note from the earlier calendar: Required stop. Pokémon Center SKYTREE TOWN opens at 10:00. An August Pokémon adventure and bingo rally is scheduled throughout Solamachi; participate only within this protected block.

title: Pokémon Center Shibuya
notes:
The trip’s single official Pokémon Center: a technology-themed flagship with Mewtwo and the Pokémon Design Lab, beside Nintendo Tokyo.

Saved note from the earlier calendar: Inside Shibuya PARCO 6F; opens 10:00. Planned with Nintendo Tokyo to avoid extra travel.

title: Shibuya lunch & cooling break
notes: Protect a seated lunch and indoor break before the afternoon crowds and festival road closures.

title: Hachikō Memorial Statue
notes: Required handwritten-list stop; quick photo before the evening Shibuya circuit.

title: MEGA Don Quijote Shibuya
notes: Required handwritten-list stop. Allow an hour for the multi-floor flagship store.

title: Indoor rest & early snack
notes: Stay inside during road restrictions and arrive at Shibuya Sky early; late arrivals can be refused.

title: Early dinner before Shibuya Bon Odori
notes: Eat before the road closures and heaviest festival crowds. The festival has food trucks and stalls, but do not rely on their queues for the family’s main dinner.

title: Shibuya Sky
notes:
The trip’s primary skyline experience. Timed entry must be booked; rooftop access can close for wind, rain, lightning or abnormal heat. If the roof closes, use the indoor gallery and Shibuya PARCO rather than adding another tower.

Saved note from the earlier calendar: Book the 13:30 timed entry so the crossing, Hachikō, MEGA Don Quijote, early dinner and Shibuya Bon Odori all fit without backtracking.

title: Shibuya Bon Odori
notes: Confirmed 2026 festival from 18:00–21:30. Join the later portion after Shibuya Sky; expect road closures and very heavy station crowds.

title: Book Shibuya Sky
notes: Reserve the 13:30 timed entry. Do not book sunset on Aug 8: Shibuya Bon Odori begins at 18:00 and road restrictions begin at 16:30. Cannot book until July 24th

title: Shiomi → teamLab Planets
notes: Walk to Shiomi Station, take JR Keiyo Line to Shin-Kiba, transfer to the Yurakucho Line for Toyosu, then walk or ride one Yurikamome stop. Shift departure to 75 minutes before the booked entry.

title: teamLab Planets
notes: A barefoot immersive digital-art visit. Replace the target with the exact QR-ticket time as soon as it is booked and arrive before the admission window.
fareDetails: Select official age categories for 2 adults and teens 13 and 16

title: Toyosu brunch & cooling break
notes: Eat and rehydrate before the exposed bayfront portion of the day.

title: Odaiba Marine Park
notes: Walk the bay promenade for Rainbow Bridge and skyline views.

title: DiverCity & Unicorn Gundam
notes: See the life-size Unicorn Gundam, including the published 13:00 daytime transformation, then cool down inside DiverCity.

title: Odaiba → Azabudai Hills
notes: Take Yurikamome and subway connections; use live transit directions because the best transfer varies. Leave generous buffer for the timed Borderless entry.

title: teamLab Borderless
notes: A room-to-room digital-art museum where installations move and interact. Exact timed entry is an editable placeholder until booked.
fareDetails: Select official age categories for 2 adults and teens 13 and 16

title: Quick dinner or snack
notes: Keep this meal quick, but do not pretend the tower is next door. Leave by 18:35.

title: Azabudai Hills → Tokyo Tower
notes: Walk about 18–22 minutes if the heat is manageable; otherwise use a short taxi. This transfer was missing from the earlier agenda.

title: Tokyo Tower Main Deck
notes: Go up to the 150 m Main Deck for the classic illuminated Tokyo landmark experience. Main Deck tickets are usually available online or on arrival.

title: Roppongi Hills (optional)
notes: End-of-day option only: the giant Maman spider, public art, shops and lively streets. Skip without regret if the family is tired.

title: Forward large luggage to Osaka
location: Tokyo Bay Shiomi Prince Hotel → APA Osaka Namba
notes: Send large suitcases one day ahead. Carry only daypacks through Hakone.

title: Buy Tokyo Tower Main Deck tickets · 4 people
notes: Purchase the Main Deck tickets for two adults, one high-school student age 16 and one junior-high student age 13. This is separate from Shibuya Sky and is not covered by the recommended rail passes.

title: Book teamLab Borderless
notes: Choose a timed entry that leaves realistic transit from Odaiba; 16:00 is the working target.

title: Book teamLab Planets
notes: Book the first normal timed entry and arrive 20–30 minutes early. The ¥12,000 Premium Pass only skips the outside entry line, not waits inside, and would cost ¥48,000 for four.

title: Prebooked taxi → Tokyo Station
notes: Check out at 05:20; taxi departs 05:25–05:30. Target arrival 05:50–06:00, then enter the Tokaido Shinkansen gates and locate the platform.
fareDetails: Book with hotel/front desk; allow daypacks

title: Buy breakfast & board
notes: Buy a portable breakfast inside the gates; hotel breakfast is too late for this departure.

notes:
Reserve this exact service now. If unavailable, select the nearest earlier or later Kodama in SmartEX and recheck every downstream time.

title: Hakone Shrine, Lake Ashi & lakeside torii
notes:
Walk the forest shrine, Lake Ashi shoreline and red lakeside torii. Do not let a long photo queue derail the mountain timetable.

Saved note from the earlier calendar: Locked Hakone stop. Includes the shrine, lakeshore and torii. No Lake Ashi cruise.

title: Bus → Chokoku-no-Mori
notes: Take the bus toward Ninotaira/Chokoku-no-Mori. Use the next service if late and protect the 16:00 mountain departure.

title: Hakone Open-Air Museum
notes:
Outdoor sculpture park, Picasso Pavilion and mountain scenery. Official hours are 09:00–17:00.

Saved note from the earlier calendar: Locked Hakone stop. Official hours 09:00–17:00. Allow 1 hour 45 minutes.

Official hours 09:00–17:00. Allow 1 hour 45 minutes. Prebuy the cheaper web ticket to bypass the sales counter; there is no interior fast pass.

title: Quick museum lunch
notes: Use the museum café/restaurant and keep this to 30 minutes so the ropeway plan retains its buffer.

title: Chokoku-no-Mori → Gora → Sounzan
notes: Hakone Tozan train to Gora, then cable car to Sounzan. Take the next departure if a connection is missed.

title: Sounzan terrace & mountain views
notes: Short terrace stop before boarding the ropeway; keep the visit brief if clouds or queues build.

title: Hakone Ropeway → Owakudani
notes: The ropeway can suspend for wind, volcanic conditions or storms. If closed, abandon this segment and start the return to Odawara.

title: Owakudani volcanic valley & black eggs
notes:
See the volcanic steam landscape, viewpoints and famous black eggs. Fuji visibility is weather-dependent.

Saved note from the earlier calendar: Locked Hakone stop. Viewpoints, volcanic valley and black eggs.

title: Owakudani → Sounzan → Gora → Odawara
notes: Ropeway back by 15:20, train from Gora around 15:25, transfer at Hakone-Yumoto around 16:10. Target Odawara 16:30–17:00.

title: Odawara buffer · dinner & snacks
notes: The 60–90 minute buffer is intentional. Collect food, rehydrate and be through the gate early. Do not plan to reach Odawara later than 17:15.

title: Hikari 653 · Odawara → Shin-Osaka
notes:
Reserve this exact direct train now. A later direct fallback must be verified in live SmartEX inventory; do not rely on an unconfirmed connection.

Saved note from the earlier calendar: LOCKED TARGET. Reserve this direct train. Exact service/timetable must still be reconfirmed before booking.

title: Midosuji Line → Namba
notes: Take Osaka Metro Midosuji Line from Shin-Osaka to Namba, then walk to APA. Earlier/later metro trains are frequent.

title: Late dinner in Hozenji / Dotonbori
notes: Choose a verified late-opening restaurant near the hotel; the mountain day is too tight for a formal dinner reservation en route.

title: Hakone Tozan H-Line bus
notes: Take the H-Line bus from Odawara toward Moto-Hakone. Check the official live route/timetable shortly before travel and allow Obon road-delay buffer.

title: Hakone Freepass · 4 adult passes
notes: Buy the 2-day Odawara-origin pass after confirming buses, cable car and ropeway are operating. Covers the local transport in the locked Hakone plan; Shinkansen tickets remain separate.

title: Hakone Open-Air Museum · online ticket
notes: Recommended for the tight Hakone day. The official web ticket is cheaper and bypasses the ticket-sales counter; it is not a fast pass inside.

title: APA Hotel & Resort Osaka Namba Ekimae Tower
notes: Locked hotel · Aug 10–14. Add confirmation number.

title: Namba → Osaka Castle
notes: Walk 2 minutes to Metro Namba Exit 30, take the Midosuji Line to Hommachi, transfer to the Chuo Line, then walk to the castle park. Use the next local services.

title: Osaka Castle grounds
notes: Walk the moats, stone walls and exterior before the heat. This early block is grounds-only because the keep opens at 09:00.

title: Osaka Castle Museum interior
notes: Enter at opening only if the queue is manageable; the interior is a modern museum inside a reconstruction.

title: Kuromon Market
notes: Browse food stalls before the market winds down; this is a tasting stop rather than the main lunch.

title: Lunch & cooling break
notes: Sit down indoors before Den Den Town and the evening districts.

title: Den Den Town
notes: Osaka’s electronics, anime, games and collectables district.

title: Shinsekai & Tsutenkaku exterior
notes: Explore the retro streets and see Tsutenkaku from below; skip another paid observation deck.

title: Dotonbori & Hozenji Yokocho
notes: See the canal and neon after dark, then Hozenji’s stone lane and moss-covered statue.

title: Osaka food night
notes: Build dinner around takoyaki, okonomiyaki, kushikatsu or yakiniku. Aug 11 is Mountain Day, so reserve a family table if choosing a popular restaurant.

title: OPTIONAL · Osaka Enjoy Eco Card
notes: Current recommendation: use IC instead. Buy only if the final route requires at least four covered Osaka Metro/city-bus rides. Aug 11 holiday price is ¥620 each; Nankai is not covered.

title: Osaka Castle Museum · optional web ticket
notes: The grounds are free. If entering the reconstructed keep, a web ticket avoids the vending line but does not skip interior or elevator queues.

title: Nankai Namba → Sumiyoshi Taisha
notes: Walk about 7 minutes from APA to Nankai Namba, take the next suitable Nankai local and walk from Sumiyoshi Taisha Station. No reservation is needed.

title: Sumiyoshi Taisha
notes: Ancient shrine with a distinctive arched bridge and calm early-morning atmosphere.

title: Breakfast & transit north
notes: Eat after the shrine while travelling toward the museum.

title: Osaka Museum of Housing and Living
notes: Walk through a recreated Edo-period Osaka streetscape. Open 10:00–17:00; paid walk-up admission is normally sufficient.

title: Tenjinbashisuji Shopping Street
notes: Explore the long covered arcade and use it for a weather-proof lunch.

title: Tenjinbashisuji lunch
notes: Choose a casual local restaurant along the covered arcade.

title: Nakanoshima riverfront
notes: See the Central Public Hall and riverside architecture on the way to Umeda.

title: Umeda & Osaka Station
notes: Explore Grand Front, the station complex and underground shopping. The paid Umeda Sky deck is skipped.

title: Umeda or Namba dinner
notes: Choose dinner near the final stop or return to Namba for an easy hotel walk.

title: Forward main luggage · Osaka → Kyoto
location: APA Hotel & Resort Osaka Namba Ekimae Tower
notes: Confirm KOKO accepts takkyubin, label bags for Aug 16 delivery and keep compact overnight bags for Nara and Hiroshima. This avoids carrying full luggage through the one-night Hiroshima stay.

title: Walk → Osaka-Namba West Gate
notes: Leave the APA lobby at 05:35. The hotel lists Osaka-Namba West Gate as a two-minute walk; allow extra station-finding buffer.

title: Kintetsu holiday-timetable semi-express → Nara
notes: Aug 13 runs the weekend/holiday timetable. Target 05:57 → 06:41; backup 06:09 Rapid Express → 06:46. Neither needs a reservation.

title: Nara Park & deer
notes: See the sacred-deer landscape before tour groups arrive; keep food and paper secured.

title: Todai-ji & Great Buddha
notes: Enter the Great Buddha Hall at its summer opening and see the monumental bronze Buddha.

title: Nigatsudo
notes: Climb to the quieter temple terrace for broad views over Nara.

title: Kasuga Taisha
notes: Walk lantern-lined forest paths to the vermilion shrine.

title: Nara lunch & cooling break
notes: Take a long indoor break before the afternoon and evening festival.

title: Naramachi
notes: Historic merchant streets, machiya buildings, cafés and small shops.

title: Early dinner before Tōkae
notes: Eat before the lantern lighting; do not assume a fast dinner after the festival.

title: Nara Tōkae Lantern Festival
notes: See the lantern lighting close to Kintetsu-Nara, then leave early for sleep. The festival continues to 21:30, but the full Todai-ji night circuit is deliberately omitted. Small rain may proceed; strong wind can cancel lighting.

title: Walk → Kintetsu-Nara Station
notes: Use the direct central-Nara exit route and follow event crowd controls. This short walk is why the festival stop is kept near Kofuku-ji and Sarusawa Pond.

title: Kintetsu-Nara → Osaka-Namba
notes: Target the holiday-timetable 20:20 Rapid Express, expected around 20:56. Exact verified backup: 20:49 Rapid Express → Osaka-Namba 21:26. If the platform is crowded, use the next departure shown on the official board.

title: Namba → Shin-Osaka
notes: Leave the APA lobby at 05:55, walk to Metro Namba Exit 30 and take the Midosuji Line direct to Shin-Osaka. Allow time to find the Shinkansen gate and platform.

title: Planned Nozomi 101 · Shin-Osaka → Hiroshima
notes: Reserve an exact service now; every Nozomi is reserved-seat-only Aug 7–16. If this target is unavailable, compare nearby 07:23/07:34 candidates in live JR West inventory.
fareDetails: 4 adult rail fares; save carriage and seat numbers

title: Hiroshima Station → Hilton · leave overnight bags
notes: Taxi is fastest for four people. Leave bags before the Peace Memorial district; room check-in can wait.

title: Taxi → Hilton bag drop → Peace Park
notes: Drop the compact Hiroshima bags at Hilton, then continue by taxi to the Dome. If traffic threatens the 11:30 museum slot, use Hiroshima Station lockers and go directly to Peace Park.

title: Shima Hospital hypocenter marker
notes: Five-minute context stop about 170 metres from the A-Bomb Dome.

title: Atomic Bomb Dome & Peace Memorial Park
notes:
Walk the Dome, riverbank, cenotaph and Children’s Peace Monument before the timed museum visit.

Saved note from the earlier calendar: Start with the Dome, Children’s Peace Monument, cenotaph and memorial park before the indoor memorials.

title: Exhibit Facility for Atomic-Bombed Remnants
notes: Free, compact underground remains of the neighbourhood that occupied this site before the bombing.

title: Hiroshima National Peace Memorial Hall
notes: Free and immediately beside the museum. Keep this in the agenda.

title: Peace Memorial Museum
notes: Allow at least two hours for the powerful artefacts, photographs and personal testimony. Aug 8–16 admission is online-reservation-only in principle.

title: Hiroshima lunch & decompression
notes: Protect a seated lunch and emotional reset after the museum.

title: Hiroshima okonomiyaki lunch · Nagata-ya
notes: Must-try Hiroshima food beside Peace Park. Expect an Obon queue; fallback is Okonomimura or Ekimae Hiroba.

title: Hondori covered arcade
notes: Efficient shaded link through central Hiroshima before Shukkeien.

title: Shukkeien Garden
notes:
Compact historic landscape garden and a calm counterpoint to the memorial district. Last entry is 17:30 in August.

Saved note from the earlier calendar: One-hour full garden circuit. Summer hours run until 18:00.

title: Hilton dinner · included in booking
notes: Your Hilton rate includes dinner and breakfast. Confirm dining venue and seating time with the hotel.

title: Reserve Hiroshima okonomiyaki dinner
notes: Venue is not yet confirmed. Reserve a family table for the city’s layered okonomiyaki because this is Obon Friday.

title: Kansai–Hiroshima Area Pass · 4 adults
notes: Purchase immediately through JR West and reserve the Aug 14 and Aug 16 Shinkansen seats. Activate Aug 14; valid through Aug 18. Pay ¥100 Miyajima visitor tax per person.

title: Hilton Hiroshima
notes: Locked hotel · add confirmation number.

title: Book Peace Memorial Museum
notes: Online timed reservation is required during Aug 8–16 and capacity is limited. The museum “premium” ticket only adds a shop voucher—it is not priority entry.

title: Taxi → Hiroshima Station
notes:
Leave Hilton by taxi with takeaway breakfast. This earlier start is required to make the first practical ferry connection.

title: Takeaway breakfast
notes: Ask Hilton about a boxed option and buy backup food on Aug 14; a sit-down hotel breakfast is too late.

notes: The first connection is tight: target the 05:52 JR service and 06:25 ferry. If either is missed, take the next practical train and the 07:05 ferry; move the shrine block later rather than rushing.

title: Itsukushima Shrine & Great Torii
notes:
Visit the over-water shrine and monumental torii before large crowds. If using the 07:05 ferry fallback, begin around 07:30 and shift the next two stops.

Saved note from the earlier calendar: First, uncrowded shrine visit while the tide rises from the 05:13 low. Return briefly at the 11:10 high tide.

title: Daisho-in Temple
notes:
Hillside Buddhist complex with statues, prayer wheels and shaded paths.

title: Walk → Momijidani Ropeway Station
notes: Walk through Momijidani; the free shuttle is suspended. Allow extra time in heat and do not assume an instant ropeway boarding.

title: Mount Misen
notes:
Use the ropeway and choose Shishiiwa only or the summit based on heat and queues. If the ropeway closes or heat is severe, skip the mountain and extend Daisho-in, Omotesando and the shrine high-tide revisit.

Saved note from the earlier calendar: Default to the ropeway and Shishiiwa viewpoint. Continue to the exposed summit only if heat and visibility are acceptable; the tide return has priority.

title: High-tide Torii shoreline revisit

title: Miyajima lunch

title: Miyajima streets & waterfront
notes: Browse Omotesando and return to the shrine waterfront if you want the higher-tide view.

notes: JR ferry and Sanyo Line. Return before the late-afternoon rush and protect hotel-break time.

title: Second Hiroshima dinner
notes: Choose a different local speciality or a relaxed hotel-area meal after Miyajima.

notes: Take subway/bus or a short taxi using live conditions. Target hotel arrival by 20:30 to protect sleep before Arashiyama.

title: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove
notes: Walk the short bamboo path before day-trip crowds arrive.

title: Togetsukyo Bridge & riverside
notes: Morning river and mountain scenery around the iconic bridge.

notes: Major Zen temple and historic garden framed by the mountains. Opens at 08:30.

title: Arashiyama Monkey Park
notes: Steep uphill walk to macaques and city views. If a severe heat warning is active, skip it, move lunch earlier and leave for northern Kyoto before peak heat.

title: Arashiyama lunch & cooling break
notes: Eat before crossing the city to northern Kyoto.

title: Arashiyama → Kinkaku-ji
notes: Taxi is the efficient option for four people; public transit is the backup but needs more time.

title: Kinkaku-ji
notes: See the Golden Pavilion and pond circuit. Expect afternoon crowds and sun exposure.

title: Kinkaku-ji → Ryoan-ji
notes: Allow 30 minutes for the short bus/taxi transfer and queues; the old agenda allowed only 10 minutes.

title: Ryoan-ji
notes: Contemplate the celebrated Zen rock garden and shaded temple grounds.

title: Cooling break & return to hotel
notes: Do not add Nishiki here; it was moved to Aug 16 before shop closing time.

title: Taxi → Kyoto Station
notes: Allow time for the station and any oversized-baggage seat check.

title: Planned Nozomi 80 · Kyoto → Tokyo

title: Marunouchi Line → Shinjuku-gyoemmae
notes: Take the Marunouchi Line from Tokyo Station and walk from Shinjuku-gyoemmae. Leave bags before sightseeing.

title: Shinjuku lunch
notes: Eat near the hotel before the garden.

title: Shinjuku Gyoen
notes: Large landscaped garden beside the hotel area. August hours are 09:00–18:00; paid admission is normally walk-up.

title: Shinjuku-sanchome shopping
notes: Department stores, cafés and indoor shopping before the neon evening.

title: Shinjuku at night
notes: Walk Omoide Yokocho, Kabukicho’s main public streets, Godzilla Head and Kabukicho Tower. Ignore touts.

title: Shinjuku dinner
notes: Choose a family-size restaurant rather than tiny Omoide Yokocho counters.

title: Shinjuku Gyoen · direct gate entry
notes: No express pass. Scan an official e-ticket or use Suica/PASMO directly at the entrance to avoid the ticket counter.

title: Cava House
notes: Locked hotel · add confirmation number.

title: Hanazono Shrine & Shinjuku morning lanes
notes: Early walk from Cava House before the shopping districts open. Add breakfast near Shinjuku-sanchome.

title: Shinjuku-gyoemmae → Otemachi
location: Imperial Palace East Gardens · Ote-mon Gate
notes: Walk from Cava House to Shinjuku-gyoemmae, take the Marunouchi Line to Otemachi and walk to Ote-mon Gate. Use the next available subway service.

title: Shinjuku-sanchome → Ikebukuro
notes: Primary: Tokyo Metro Fukutoshin Line, direct and normally about 10 minutes, with frequent service. Backup: JR Yamanote Line from Shinjuku Station. No reservation.

title: animate Ikebukuro Flagship
notes: Official hours currently 10:00–21:00. Start at opening before the busiest part of the day.

title: Otemachi lunch & cooling break
notes: Use a long indoor lunch before the west-Tokyo afternoon.

title: Sunshine City & Bandai Namco Cross Store
notes: Indoor teen-focused block for Bandai Namco Cross Store, gachapon and character shops. Pokémon Center Mega Tokyo is currently closed until further notice—visit it only if the official store page confirms reopening.

title: Ikebukuro lunch
notes: Eat before transferring west. Sunshine City has many air-conditioned family options.

title: Ikebukuro → Nakano
notes: Primary: JR Saikyo Line to Shinjuku, then JR Chuo-Sobu local or Chuo Rapid to Nakano. Backup: JR Yamanote to Takadanobaba, then Tokyo Metro Tozai Line to Nakano. Allow about 35–40 minutes including the transfer; no reservation.

title: Nakano Broadway & Sun Mall
notes: Allow nearly three hours because Mandarake operates more than 30 specialist departments. Individual store hours vary; this afternoon block is safer than an early visit.

title: Nakano → Koenji
location: Nakano Station, Tokyo → Koenji Station, Tokyo
notes: Take a JR Chuo-Sobu local one stop. Rapid trains may skip Koenji depending on the day and time, so check the platform display. Frequent service; no reservation.

title: Ikebukuro or Shinjuku dinner
notes: Eat in Ikebukuro or return to Shinjuku for a late local evening.

title: Koenji shopping streets & dinner
location: Koenji Station / PAL and LOOK shopping streets, Tokyo
notes: Walk the vintage and record-shop streets, then eat locally. Finish by walking south through PAL and LOOK toward Shin-Koenji Station.

title: Koenji → Cava House
location: Shin-Koenji Station → Shinjuku-gyoemmae Station → Cava House
notes: Primary: walk to Shin-Koenji Station and take the Tokyo Metro Marunouchi Line direct to Shinjuku-gyoemmae, then walk to Cava House. Backup: JR Chuo-Sobu local from Koenji to Shinjuku, then taxi.

title: Shinjuku-gyoemmae → Tsukiji
notes: Walk from Cava House to Shinjuku-gyoemmae, take the Marunouchi Line to Ginza and transfer to the Hibiya Line for Tsukiji. Use the next available services.

title: Tsukiji Outer Market
notes: Breakfast at specifically verified early-opening stalls; general visitor shopping improves around 09:00 and official guidance recommends 09:00–14:00.

title: Hamarikyu Gardens
notes: Tidal landscape garden and teahouse scenery. Corrected from 08:45 because the garden opens at 09:00.

title: Ginza
notes: Flagship shops, department-store food halls and modern architecture.

title: Ginza lunch & cooling break
notes: Take an indoor lunch before the final shopping block.

title: Tokyo Station & Character Street
notes: See the restored red-brick exterior, then underground character and souvenir stores.

notes: Required handwritten-list stop. Exterior plaza and bridge view; East Gardens are normally closed Fridays, so this avoids relying on garden access.
